place.source_title: Paxton Water Tower, Centre & Market Streets

brief: Tall octagonal brick standpipe water tower of the 1880s with arched panels and a corbelled top, beside a small brick pump house. Record gap: no photographs; 4 measured drawing sheets (plan, elevations, section).

facade.notes: the Paxton IL water tower (1887-88), HABS axonometric: an 80 ft octagonal brick tower with lancet windows and corbelled top courses, which once carried an 18 ft wooden tank on four interior timber columns (tank removed in the 1940s); a long gabled pump house attached; on a town lot near the centre (site plan)

why.note: a town's first waterworks (1880s): a pump house and a masonry tower carrying the tank
